correctness.rationale: Conditioning on disjoint pair totals gives Cov(g_theta(K),g_phi(L)). The increment g_theta(k+1)-g_theta(k)=delta E sgn(S_k)+P(S_k=0) is nonnegative by a monotone coupling to fair signs. Conditional L given K=k is Bin(N-k,v/(1-u)), so h(k)=E[g_phi(L)|K=k] is decreasing and the extreme total pairs force strict negative covariance for every N. Stirling and Chernoff imply L2 binomial local-linearizations with slopes 1/sqrt(2 pi N u) for balanced pairs, and |delta| for biased pairs. Multiplication by Cov(K,L)=-Nuv gives each leading coefficient; all remainder bounds fit the stated order. The included standard-library code passed 72 exact rational finite checks in six profiles. Finite checks are not infinite proofs.

General multinomial negative-dependence ordering can yield components of the sign argument, not the three-order sharp asymptotic classification with all profile parameters. Targeted mathematical-record and web comparisons found no directly covering full theorem. Planned general-reference variance work is unavailable, and implicit coverage elsewhere remains a risk.

value.rationale: The previously identified disjoint-edge covariance survives at constant order in a uniform multinomial histogram despite uncorrelated raw increments. For arbitrary fixed probabilities this theorem proves strict negative finite-sample covariance and discovers two higher-order asymptotic regimes with sharp coefficients, separated exactly by local pair-balance equalities. These regimes matter in covariance decompositions for uncentered ordered-histogram total variation and cannot be substituted by the existing single uniform constant. The result does not claim an effect for centered nonuniform reference statistics or adjacent edges.
